body:
A few extra things:

- This only happens with next dev --turbo, not when built or ran without turbopack
- It also only happens when the route with only a folder is the most recent page visited. If you type in another route that exists and the go back to the non-existant route, and then back again, which would normally download the file, it works as expected.
In my case it is caused by NextJS cache

I experience the same behavior.
There is no problem when navigating through the menu and links on the website. I can return to any page with no problems.

But as soon as I change the URL manually, there are problems.

Instead of going back, it downloads a file with the name of the route/segment I want to go back to.

### To Reproduce
1. Open `https://example.com/page1`
2. Modify URL by hand to `https://example.com/page2`
3. Click on Back Button
**Result:** Downloading a file named `page1` which contains a similar structure like  `J0:[["children","",["",{}],null,null]]`

(If I change the URL and start navigating the site, I can return to any page. Everything works as expected. But as soon as I reach the point in history where the URL was changed, a file downloads.)

Any ideas why this is happening?

#### additional infos:
- Locelhost doesn't show this behavior. It happens only when deployed.
- I am not using 'next dev --turbo'
- only happens when modifing URL manually
- using appDir

Adding these to layout.js fixes this:
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
export const revalidate = 0

Source: https://beta.nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/segment-config

issue.title: turbopack: add vary header to app routes
issue.body:
Next.js adds a `Vary: RSC, Next-Router-State-Tree, Next-Router-Prefetch` to app routes for both rendering and flight requests. Without this, the browser can mistakenly serve the flight request to the app render, and vice versa.

This only adds `Vary: RSC` for the moment, I'm not sure what the others are used for. We also don't add a `Cache-Control: max-age=0` header, but I'm not sure if that's necessary either.

Fixes NEXT-657
